findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects in this reports bucket are stored without enforced SSE-KMS/AES256 encryption at rest.

No ACL is specified and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or policy restricts access, so the bucket relies on defaults and can be made publicly readable/writable by any ACL or policy change without guardrails.
Versioning is disabled, so objects (including the seeded vendor roster) can be silently overwritten or deleted with no recovery, removing tamper evidence for data stored in this bucket.
No logging block is configured, so read/write access to this bucket is not recorded to the audit_trail bucket, hindering detection and forensic investigation of unauthorized access.
This ledger export bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving sensitive financial export data unencrypted at rest.
Versioning is not enabled, so ledger export objects can be overwritten or deleted without recovery or tamper evidence.
No logging block is configured for this ledger bucket, so access to sensitive financial data is not auditable.
The model artifacts bucket lacks a server_side_encryption_configuration block, so proprietary artifacts are stored without enforced server-side encryption.
The runbooks bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration; operational runbooks frequently contain hostnames, procedures, and secrets and are stored unencrypted at rest.
No logging block is configured, so access to operational runbook content is not recorded for audit or intrusion detection.
The audit log destination bucket does not itself log access, so an attacker reading or tampering with centralized logs leaves no record.

A vendor roster spreadsheet (likely containing third-party contact/PII data) is uploaded with no server_side_encryption or kms_key_id argument into a bucket that also lacks default encryption, so the object is stored in plaintext.
